[+] Accounts whose owner stayed stable continued to expand at healthy rates - Expansion rate for accounts with no owner change is computable from the same revenue model

- Uncovered claim 'Expansion revenue from existing customers declined noticeably this year' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts a measurable decline in expansion revenue (a headline/margin segment) year-over-year. No drafted criterion measures this. core_vs_headline_growth can express a decline in the expansion segment relative to core revenue, but it is not present among the criteria. AC1 (post_change_revenue_decline) measures the ownership-churn differential, not the aggregate year-over-year expansion decline. The aggregate decline is a distinct substance that no existing criterion covers. (consider check: core_vs_headline_growth)
Drafted 2 criteria: AC1, AC2
Coverage guard: 1 note(s) - proceeding:

[note] Uncovered claim 'The decline occurred in accounts where the AE relationship had changed hands recently' [PARAMETRIC]: The existing check post_change_revenue_decline is precisely designed to measure a revenue decline that tracks a relationship/ownership change event. The drafted AC2 uses this check but only constrains the gap between stable and reassigned accounts (min_gap_pp: 10); it does not independently assert that the decline occurred specifically in the changed-accounts segment. The claim's substance — that the decline is concentrated in recently-changed accounts — is not independently proven, and the direction/parameterization of AC2 does not pin the decline to the changed-accounts cohort as its own assertion. (consider check: post_change_revenue_decline)

This compensates for the outlier_deals change which alone would push headline deeper; the discount move keeps headline pinned inside band while the whale-share move does the gap-widening.)
